exposure: Compound Small Peptide of Chinese Medicine (CSPCM)
outcome: Intestinal immunity (secretion of IL-2, IL-22, TNF-alpha, sIgA, percent of CD3+ and CD4+ cells)
Intestinal microflora (cecal flora taxa, abundance of Firmicutes, Lactobacillus, Bacteroidetes, Deferribacteres, Proteobacteria, Mucispirillum, Bacteroides, Flexisprra)
Intestinal development (length of villi, depth of crypt, area of Peyer's node)
cohort: 100 male Kunming mice were divided into a control group, a cyclophosphamide (CTX) model group, and three groups treated with different doses of CSPCM after CTX-induced immunosuppression.
finding: Cyclophosphamide significantly impaired intestinal immunity, development, and flora in mice, while Compound Small Peptide of Chinese Medicine (CSPCM) effectively ameliorated these negative effects in a dose-dependent manner.
